confirmWithMargo: FOUNDING YEAR 1997 is asserted eight times on this page (hero, story, leadership, timeline, footer). site.ts still holds foundingYear as null because the blueprint and the design disagree. One source has to win before launch.
The design says AHMEDABAD, GUJARAT in the story, manufacturing and timeline sections while its own footer says Nashik, Maharashtra. Built as Nashik, matching the confirmed address. Needs a ruling.

Unverified figures carried straight from the design: 27+ years, 1,200+ active clients, 25+ export countries, 500T monthly capacity, 98.7% on-time delivery, 80,000 sq. ft. floor area, 400+ team members, 400+ compounds, 18 yrs average senior tenure, 100% safety record, < 0.1% defect rate, 48 hr sample lead time, ±0.01 mm tolerance, ₹120 Cr+ FY 2023-24 export turnover.
Capacity conflict: this page says 500 TONNES per month; site.ts records 500,000 UNITS per month from the pack. Those are not the same measure.

Certifications claimed here that Margo does NOT hold per the pack: ISO 14001:2015, NABL-accredited lab, ISO Class 7 cleanroom, REACH and RoHS certification, FIEO Export Award 2023. The /certifications page states plainly that ISO 9001:2015 is the only management system certification held.
Named auditors (Bureau Veritas, TUV SUD, SGS India, FIEO) are unconfirmed. The real certification body is still unknown, see checklist item iso-scan.
The eight client names on the trust wall are the design's, not a supplied list. Each needs permission before a logo or name is published.
Timeline milestones for 2002 through 2024 were written to fit the design's seven-year chip row. Only 1997 came from the design. All seven need Margo's real dates.
Countries list, export turnover and 'six continents' all need confirming against the actual shipping record.
Every image on this page is stock, including both portraits. See checklist item about-photos.

green.body: Automating compound mixing and cure control cut scrap: material utilisation improved 20% and cycle time fell 30%, which is less rubber and less energy for the same part. The plant is fully compliant with MIDC environmental and industrial norms. We have not set a carbon target and will not publish one until we can measure against it.

h1: Precision Rubber, Made in Nashik Since 2005.
intro: Margo Rubber Products is a manufacturer of moulded and extruded rubber components in Nashik, Maharashtra. Certified to ISO 9001:2015 for moulded rubber components. Compound formulation, mould tooling, moulding, finishing and testing all happen under one roof, for 24 named accounts across seven sectors.

leadership.body: Reverse engineering is a standard route to a first order here. We measure the part, identify the compound family, and quote against the sample. It is also the clearest test of whether a supplier actually formulates compound or simply buys it in.
quoteLines: A large share of our work arrives as a worn part in an envelope, not a CAD file.
Somebody needs that part to exist again, and it has to fit.

manufacturing.body: A 10,000+ sq ft plant in the Nashik industrial belt, laid out for a single linear workflow with compression, transfer and injection moulding plus continuous-cure extrusion. Automated presses hold cure temperature and pressure closed-loop, which takes operator variation out of the part.
equipment: Automated moulding presses — closed-loop temperature and pressure control
Digital curing ovens — programmable, with a retrievable cure record per batch
Compound mixing, automated — even filler distribution, batch after batch
In-line deflashing and trimming — consistent finish, less manual handling
IoT production monitoring — a slow press shows up the same day, not at month end
Centralised ERP and MES — planning, tracking and batch traceability across the plant

paragraphs: Margo Rubber Products was founded in Nashik in 2005. The previous works ran 6,000 sq ft and about 200,000 parts a month. Moving to a purpose-built 10,000+ sq ft plant, and automating during the move, took installed capacity to five million parts a month — twenty-five times the old works.

The plant is built for a single linear workflow: raw material in at one end, finished goods out at the other, with no cross-traffic between clean and flash-generating areas. Today it supplies 24 named accounts across automotive, industrial machinery, electrical, specialist vehicles, medical, chemicals and tooling.
